blindSummary:
This country is legally improved but socially dangerous for trans visitors. The High Court struck down the colonial-era sodomy laws in a 2018 ruling, upheld on appeal, removing criminalisation of same-sex intimacy; but there is no legal gender recognition, no SOGI anti-discrimination protection, and parliament has repeatedly rejected reforms (the governing party's constitution review again refused SOGI protections in 2024).

Documented street risk is substantial: community advocates report trans people are still being beaten, stoned and hacked, with most incidents never reported; and police have publicly warned of a spate of ambush robberies lured through a geolocation dating app — criminals using fake profiles to lure LGBT victims to meetings followed by armed robbery (multiple cases through 2023-2024, including a man beaten and robbed in a suburb of the capital). This dating-app predation pattern is a direct traveler concern.
blindOutOfScope: Decriminalisation status and reform rejections are climate/legal context; no trans-specific statute exists.
blindSourceSummaries: A national daily (July 2024): reporting on how far there is yet to go for recognition and safe spaces - the director of the national transgender coalition says the trans community is the most marginalised and is not even recognised in the country; gender identity is not recognised separately from sexual orientation; gender-identity markers on institutional forms are absent; national discussions and attitudinal research needed.

A national daily (Nov 2024): police warning over cyber criminals - dating-app hook-ups ending in stolen cars, cash and phones; criminals create fake dating accounts to lure LGBT+ victims into meetings followed by armed robbery, beatings or sexual assault; two separate incidents reported in one week.

A national daily editorial (June 2024): an editorial calling for an end to dating-app hate attacks - a spate of app-related attacks (almost half a dozen in recent months); a police superintendent points to gaps in the law: there is no specific hate-crime category in legislation; the editorial argues the gap must be closed.

Local news site (Aug 2024): the head of a national LGBT-rights coalition unhappy that LGBTQ rights reform was ignored again - the governing party's constitution review committee rejected reform of sexual-orientation rights; the coalition had recommended adding sexual orientation and gender identity to protected statuses under the fundamental-rights section of the constitution; no political party has stepped up, it noted.

An LGBT travel-news community guide (Aug 2012): although homosexuality is illegal, 'the laws are mostly ignored' - context of the country's history, from its first overseas colonisation through rule by a later colonial power.

LGBTQ news outlet (Nov 2017): first-person account by a gay man calling himself a criminal simply for being gay - his High Court challenge to this country's laws (up to 25 years for 'serious indecency'); ~100,000 LGBT people live under the threat; the laws were inherited from the former colonial power but extended to lesbians after independence.

An international decriminalisation news campaign (June 2016): the prime minister said the state must protect all citizens whatever the identity of their partners, but said there were no plans to amend the sodomy laws and declined to address the national equal-opportunity body's call for anti-discrimination protection.
blindLocalsOnly: No legal gender recognition and no SOGI anti-discrimination protection — resident-facing; the pattern of beatings, stonings and machete attacks describes residents.
blindTangential: The dating-app ambush robbery pattern is a direct risk for trans visitors using apps.
